summary.title: DevSecOps basics: 9 tips for shifting left
summary.one_liner: You learn how to move security earlier into the software development lifecycle (shift left) by fostering dev-security collaboration and automating security scans.
keywords: how to bring security earlier in development
takeaways: Shifting left means moving security testing from the end of the development pipeline to near the beginning.
Security and development teams should audit tools and responsibilities together and define security objectives at every SDLC stage.
Automating SAST on every commit and integrating scans into developer workflows finds vulnerabilities at their source.
Giving developers access to SAST and DAST reports and keeping changes small helps secure code and reduce review burden.
Clear documentation of role changes, security training, and a security champions program support a DevSecOps culture.
summary.summary: This GitLab blog post, the first in a five-part DevSecOps series, argues that security testing often starts too late and that dev and security teams frequently disagree on ownership. It cites findings from GitLab's 2020 Global DevSecOps Survey and a Ponemon Institute report to illustrate the problem. The article then lists nine practical tips, such as auditing tools together, automating SAST at every commit, building scans into developer workflows, and streamlining the toolchain. It also points to a DevSecOps Maturity Assessment for self-evaluation.
